# honest-cv

[![CI](https://github.com/OWNER/honest-cv/actions/workflows/ci.yml/badge.svg)](https://github.com/OWNER/honest-cv/actions/workflows/ci.yml)
[![License: MIT](https://img.shields.io/badge/license-MIT-blue.svg)](LICENSE)

**Honest, ATS-safe CVs tailored to each role, generated by your AI agent.** honest-cv is an MCP
server, a CLI and a Claude Code skill. It keeps one source of truth about your experience and
turns it into a PDF and DOCX for each type of role. It never claims a skill you don't have.

[Leer en español](README.es.md)

![Demo: score a job post, build a variant, verify it](docs/assets/demo.gif)

## Why

Many CVs that get no callbacks don't fail on design. They fail on targeting, and on details that
quietly break text extraction. AI makes the opposite problem easy: a model will happily stuff a CV
with keywords you can't defend in an interview. honest-cv is built around three ideas:

- **The code enforces honesty, not a prompt.** Every skill has a level. A skill at familiarity
  level is always labeled as such, and a skill you don't have is never printed. Raising a level
  takes written evidence and *your* confirmation, which the server asks you for directly. The
  model can't confirm on your behalf.
- **Gaps are measured against your own inventory.** For each keyword a job post asks for,
  honest-cv tells you which of three cases it is:
  - you have it, but this CV doesn't show it;
  - you only know it at familiarity level;
  - you don't have it.
- **ATS safety is checked on every build.** Every PDF goes through two text extractors (pypdf and
  pdfminer.six). The build checks that the text is one column, has no ligatures, keeps each date on
  its role's line, follows the right reading order and includes every bullet.

The server is deterministic and needs no API key. Your MCP client's model runs the conversation;
honest-cv validates, builds, verifies and measures. Your data stays on your machine.

## Quick start

honest-cv needs [uv](https://docs.astral.sh/uv/). Typst and the fonts ship inside the package,
so there is nothing else to install.

### Claude Code

```bash
claude mcp add honest-cv -- uvx honest-cv serve --profile ~/cv-profile
```

To install the skill as well, which guides the interview and the tailoring:

```bash
mkdir -p ~/.claude/skills/honest-cv
curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/OWNER/honest-cv/main/skills/honest-cv/SKILL.md \
  -o ~/.claude/skills/honest-cv/SKILL.md
```

Then start with *"interview me for my CV"*, or run `/mcp__honest-cv__interview`.

### Cursor

Add this to `~/.cursor/mcp.json`, or to `.cursor/mcp.json` in a project:

```json
{
  "mcpServers": {
    "honest-cv": {
      "command": "uvx",
      "args": ["honest-cv", "serve", "--profile", "/absolute/path/to/cv-profile"]
    }
  }
}
```

### Claude Desktop

Edit `claude_desktop_config.json`:
- on macOS, `~/Library/Application Support/Claude/`;
- on Windows, `%APPDATA%\Claude\`.

Add the same `mcpServers` block as in the Cursor example and restart the app. If the app can't
find `uvx`, use its absolute path (`which uvx`).

> **Skill upgrades need a client that supports MCP elicitation**, so the server can ask you to
> confirm. On a client that doesn't support it, the server refuses the upgrade and gives you a
> command to run in a terminal instead: `honest-cv skill <profile> "<name>" <level> --evidence "..."`.

## Your profile

A profile is a folder with four YAML files. Create one with `honest-cv init ~/cv-profile`, or let
the `interview` prompt fill it in with you. Keep it out of public repositories.

| File | What it holds |
|---|---|
| `profile.yaml` | Contact details, roles, education, certifications and languages. |
| `bullets.yaml` | A pool of achievements, each with an `id`, a `role` and `tags`. |
| `skills.yaml` | Your skill inventory, with levels and evidence. |
| `variants.yaml` | One CV plan per type of role. A variant can inherit from another with `extends:`. |

Any text can be a single string or one string per language: `{en: ..., es: ...}`. CVs can be
built in English and in Spanish.

| Level | Meaning | On the CV |
|---|---|---|
| `P` | Used in production at a job | Shown |
| `L` | Your own project or lab | Shown |
| `F` | Familiarity | Only on the line labeled "Familiarity" |
| `X` | You don't have it | Never shown, but recorded so gap reports are honest |

See [`examples/ada/`](examples/ada/) for a complete, fictional profile with three variants, a job
post and its keywords.

## CLI

```bash
honest-cv init ~/cv-profile                        # create the profile templates
honest-cv build ~/cv-profile -v backend -l en -l es # PDF + DOCX, verified on every build
honest-cv verify any-cv.pdf --text                  # check any PDF, even one made elsewhere
honest-cv score ~/cv-profile -k "Kubernetes,Go" -p "Rust"   # coverage per variant, with gaps
honest-cv skill ~/cv-profile "Rust" L --evidence "CLI tool on GitHub"  # asks you to confirm
honest-cv serve --profile ~/cv-profile              # the MCP server, over stdio
```

`verify` works on any PDF. Use `--text` to see exactly what a parser extracts. Its
`single_column` check also catches a common defect: a date aligned to the right, which parsers
split away from its role.

## MCP tools and prompts

| Name | What it does |
|---|---|
| `init_profile` | Creates a profile folder with commented templates. |
| `get_inventory` | Returns your skills, grouped by level, with years and evidence. |
| `set_skill` | Adds or changes a skill. To raise its level it needs evidence and asks you to confirm. |
| `add_bullet` | Adds an achievement to the pool. |
| `list_variants` | Lists the variants after inheritance, with their bullet texts and the bullets no variant uses. |
| `build_cv` | Renders a PDF and/or DOCX and verifies it. |
| `verify_pdf` | Runs the ATS checks on any PDF and returns its extracted text. |
| `score_job` | Measures the keyword coverage of each variant. The client extracts the keywords. |
| `gap_report` | Groups missing keywords by what you can honestly do about each one. |
| prompt `interview` | Fills your inventory and bullet pool, one question at a time. |
| prompt `tailor_for_job` | Scores the variants, explains the gaps, adapts a variant and rebuilds. |

## ATS guarantees

The template enforces these. `verify` checks them on every build, and the test suite runs in CI on
Linux, macOS and Windows:

- One column. No layout tables, images, icons, headers or footers.
- Ligatures off, no hyphenation, and terms like "CI/CD" never split across lines.
- Reading order equals source order. Dates sit on the same line as their role.
- Text is extractable by both pypdf and pdfminer.six, and the two agree.
- The fonts (Carlito, metric-compatible with Calibri) are embedded and identical on every machine.

## Development

```bash
uv sync
uv run pytest
uv run honest-cv build examples/ada -l en -l es
```

The repository's `.mcp.json` registers `honest-cv-dev` with the fictional profile, so Claude Code
in this folder can use your working copy. See [CONTRIBUTING.md](CONTRIBUTING.md).
